Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. Title: Diagnosis of test `testRead7ZipMultiVolumeArchiveForStream`

Details: The test `testRead7ZipMultiVolumeArchiveForStream` in `Maven221MultiVolumeTest` attempts to read entries from a multi-volume ZIP archive stream using `ZipArchiveInputStream`. It expects to raise an `IOException` with the message `"Truncated ZIP file"` when reading from a truncated entry in the archive. The failure occurs because the test did not get this exception and instead was able to read from the truncated entry, violating the intended behavior, as indicated by the fail message at line 97.

The classes involved in handling ZIP archive input streaming that are covered by the failing test include `ZipArchiveInputStream` and several of its methods such as:
- Constructor `ZipArchiveInputStream(InputStream, String, boolean)`
- `getNextEntry()`
- `read(byte[], int, int)`
- `close()`
- `closeEntry()`
- `fill()`
- `readFully(byte[])`

The fundamental issue lies in when and how `ZipArchiveInputStream.read()` handles truncated entries. The test expects an exception when reading from a truncated ZIP entry but instead it successfully reads without error.

To narrow down the root cause, it is logical to review the implementation of these methods in `ZipArchiveInputStream` to understand:
1. How `getNextEntry()` moves to the next entry and detects truncation.
2. How `read()` behaves on a truncated entry and whether it throws the expected `IOException`.
3. How the reading logic fills internal buffers (`fill()`), closes entries (`closeEntry()`), and performs full reads (`readFully(byte[])`) since these likely interact during streaming.

Next, I will retrieve the code snippet of the constructor `ZipArchiveInputStream(InputStream, String, boolean)` to see how the stream is initialized.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
